To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the factorial hidden Markov model (HMM) is an appropriate probabilistic model for high-dimensional data with spatial structure; 2) the factorization of the likelihood function in the factorial HMM allows for the development of efficient approximate inference algorithms; and 3) the approximate algorithms are provably accurate in the sense that their error is `dimension free'.

(a) we propose algorithms for approximate smoothing and filtering for high-dimensional factorial HMMs; (b) we prove that the error bounds for the approximations are `dimension free'; (c) we prove that a key step in the approximation involves discarding likelihood factors according to a notion of locality; (d) the factorial structure of the HMM likelihood arises naturally when data has known spatial structure; (e) the new algorithms are demonstrated on synthetic and real-world examples.

we have proposed a new algorithm that is able to perform approximate filtering and smoothing on high-dimensional data, and we have proved the algorithm's accuracy does not necessarily degrade as the dimension of the data increases.
